title: Triage latency spikes across Hosted / Dedicated / Private - urgent runtime mitigation
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments have reported intermittent, high-severity latency regressions (TTFT spike and sustained tokens/sec drop) when serving long-context generation (models with context > 4k tokens) and mixed-size request workloads. Impact surfaced 2026-03-11 evening UTC; elevated PagerDuty alerts and two enterprise escalations (one Dedicated customer + one Private deployment).

Observed symptoms:
- TTFT increases 3x for affected requests; tokens/sec throughput drops by 40-60% on the same machines.
- Spike is bursty and correlates with a mix of long-context streaming requests plus background KV-cache priming in the same GPU pool.
- Affected across deployments (hosted regional clusters, dedicated GPU pools, and one VPC customer).
- Canary and smaller models are largely unaffected; regression appears for a family of 4k+ context model variants and sharded quantized kernels.

Initial investigation notes:
- Runtime traces show increased kernel selection fallback to a slow path when sequence length distribution crosses a threshold; observed additional CPU-side serialization when KV cache eviction coincides with new prefix loads.
- Scheduler queues show head-of-line blocking when a long-stream request enters batching; requests behind become starved and latency balloons.
- Host OS metrics on one Dedicated pool showed periodic cgroup CPU throttling on inference helper processes during bursts (suspected mis-set CPU shares after an autoscaling event).
- No obvious model parameter change or deployment rollout timed with the onset (no release coincident).

Immediate mitigation actions (done / in-flight):
- Implemented temporary routing rule in control plane to divert new long-context requests for affected model variants to a lower-latency quantized fallback model in Hosted regions (deployed 2026-03-13 03:12 UTC). This reduced customer error rate and average TTFT for those customers by ~35% within 30 minutes.
- Applied an emergency scheduler config change to prioritize short-running requests in Dedicated pools and reduce batch depth for long-streams (rolled to 2 Dedicated pools; monitoring ongoing).
- Worked with an on-prem customer ops contact to increase CPU shares for inference helpers in their VPC nodes (temporary tweak; they reported immediate improvement).

Planned short-term fixes (next 72 hours):
1) Patch kernel-selection logic to avoid unnecessary fallback to the slow path when sequence length slightly exceeds previous thresholds; target PR and canary by 2026-03-15.
2) Add preemptive scheduler guard that isolates long streaming sessions into a separate execution lane to avoid head-of-line blocking; roll to Hosted canaries 2026-03-16.
3) Add per-queue tokens-per-second and TTFT percentile metrics to Console dashboards for affected models and pools (observability runbook update 2026-03-14).

Long-term action items (next quarter):
- Revisit autoscaling CPU share reconciliation after scaling events to avoid helper process throttling.
- Formalize long-request isolation policy in scheduler and document guidelines for customers on long-context usage and recommended routing.
- Add fuzz/regression tests in CI that simulate mixed short+long workloads to catch throughput regressions pre-deploy.

Acceptance criteria:
- Immediate mitigations keep customer-facing TTFT under SLA for reported customers and prevent further escalations.
- Kernel-selection patch reduces fallback occurrences in canaries by >80% for same workload.
- Scheduler lane reduces head-of-line blocking O(1) incidents in Dedicated pools for one week of traffic.

Notes / constraints:
- Any runtime change must be validated in Hosted canaries before Dedicated rollouts; Private customers require coordination for upgrades/patching windows.
- Temporary routing may increase unit cost for routed traffic; notify billing and customer success teams.
